title: Mind the gap: from plausible to valid self-explanations in large language models
status: Published journal article; supplied full PDF
evidence_url: Supplied PAPER 2.pdf, sections 3–6 and Appendix H
access_depth: Full supplied paper plus README and selected implementation source
contribution: Analyses extractive/counterfactual self-explanations of LLM classifiers; samples edited inputs and explicitly reclassifies them; estimates retries and evaluates validity, similarity, dependability and runtime.
limitations: Classification-only; decoder-only; gradient tests up to 9B; no actionability assessment; prompt sensitivity not systematically evaluated; finite retry budget can fail; similarity/validity do not establish internal reasoning.
relevance: Direct base paper and mandatory methodological reference.
baseline_use: Reproduce target-model reclassification baseline and bounded rejection sampling before claiming a better validator. Report candidate attempts and failures.

title: LLMs Don’t Know Their Own Decision Boundaries: The Unreliability of Self-Generated Counterfactual Explanations
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
status: Conference paper identified by official ACL XML and author repository
access_depth: Official abstract/metadata plus author README; full paper not retrieved
contribution: Studies self-generated counterfactual explanations against empirically elicited LLM decision boundaries; observes a validity–minimality trade-off when prompting for counterfactuals versus minimal counterfactuals.
limitations: README identifies tabular binary-classification setting; do not present these results as text-CF evidence or infer complete paper limitations from abstract alone. No numerical effect size asserted here.
relevance: Strong near prior art: obtaining valid edits is insufficient; minimality and genuine boundary correspondence need evaluation.
baseline_use: Prompt-only counterfactual and minimal-counterfactual conditions are valuable controls; tabular exhaustive-boundary metric does not transfer unchanged to free text.

title: Explaining NLP Models via Minimal Contrastive Editing (MiCE)
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL-IJCNLP 2021
status: Conference Findings paper; official ACL metadata and author repository
access_depth: Official metadata plus README and selected search implementation; full paper not retrieved
contribution: Uses a trained editor and search over masking amounts to find minimal contrastive edits; source re-scores candidates with the target predictor, records successful target-label edits and uses a bounded beam/search procedure.
limitations: Original toolkit uses task-specific predictor/editor training and legacy AllenNLP/Python3.7 setup; not a drop-in modern instruction-LLM experiment. No benchmark results were rerun.
relevance: Minimality search plus classifier validation existed before LLM self-CF work.
baseline_use: Relevant algorithmic comparator if adapted fairly to same target model; adaptation must be disclosed.
code_licence: Not verified: conventional LICENSE/LICENSE.md/LICENSE.txt paths returned404; do not infer licence

title: Polyjuice: Generating Counterfactuals for Explaining, Evaluating, and Improving Models
venue: Proceedings of the 59th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics and the 11th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing (Volume 1: Long Papers)
status: Conference paper; official ACL metadata and author repository
access_depth: Official abstract/metadata plus README; full paper not retrieved
contribution: A GPT-2-based general-purpose perturbation generator with controls over edit type and location; supports counterfactual error analysis and augmentation of explanation techniques.
limitations: Generator is distinct from validity certification for a specified classifier; sampled perturbations need target-specific label checks. Older generator/tool dependencies and text licences need consideration.
relevance: Controlled lexical/semantic edit generation is established prior art.
baseline_use: Candidate perturbation-generation comparator or robustness suite component; do not equate every perturbation with a valid counterfactual.

title: CREST: A Joint Framework for Rationalization and Counterfactual Text Generation
venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
status: Conference paper; official ACL metadata and author repository
access_depth: Official abstract/metadata plus detailed README; full paper not retrieved
contribution: Joint selective rationalization and counterfactual text generation; trains masker/editor, classifies generated edits and uses counterfactuals to regularize rationales. Repository provides IMDB/SNLI edits and validity, fluency, diversity, plausibility and simulation evaluation instructions.
limitations: Training-oriented rationalizer/predictor architecture differs from post-hoc verification of a fixed instruction LLM; off-the-shelf validity checks in README must not be assumed same-model validation. Compiler/SparseMAP and legacy dependencies add reproduction cost.
relevance: Direct prior art against novelty claims about combining rationales, evidence extraction and counterfactual generation.
baseline_use: Possible strong method/data comparator with careful target alignment; at minimum compare conceptual differences explicitly.

title: DISCO: Distilling Counterfactuals with Large Language Models
venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
status: Conference paper; official ACL metadata and author repository
access_depth: Official abstract/metadata plus author README; full paper not retrieved
contribution: Prompts a large language model for phrasal perturbations and filters generations with a task-specific teacher; counterfactual data trains more robust NLI student models.
limitations: Training-data augmentation objective, not explanation verification of the same decision LLM; teacher filtering is not automatically target-model validity. README and final ACL abstract report different effect sizes, so no numerical comparison quoted.
relevance: Generate-and-filter text pipelines with LLMs are established.
baseline_use: Useful prior art and generation/filtering control; cannot directly substitute teacher labels for target-model checks.
code_licence: Code MIT verified from LICENSE; README links/claims about data licences conflict and need separate verification

title: ERASER: A Benchmark to Evaluate Rationalized NLP Models
venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
status: Conference benchmark paper; official ACL metadata and repository
access_depth: Official abstract/metadata plus README and metric implementation; full paper not retrieved
contribution: Benchmark with human rationale annotations and distinct plausibility/faithfulness-oriented measurements. Source implements rationale alignment, classification, comprehensiveness, sufficiency and AOPC metrics.
limitations: Human rationale overlap measures agreement, not causal internal faithfulness; removal/retention metrics depend on model score access and perturbation distribution. Dataset source licences must be checked individually.
relevance: Provides evaluation protocol and potentially annotated movie-review data consistent with base paper2.
baseline_use: Candidate evaluation backbone. Label probability must be meaningfully defined for generative labels; no fabricated probability for API-only access.
code_licence: Apache-2.0 verified for code; individual data licences separate

title: Beyond Accuracy: Behavioral Testing of NLP Models with CheckList
venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
status: Conference paper; official ACL metadata and author repository
access_depth: Official abstract/metadata plus detailed README; full paper not retrieved
contribution: Behavioral test methodology over linguistic capabilities and test types, with tools for minimum functionality, invariance and directional-expectation testing.
limitations: Tests target model behavior and task-specific expectations; not a certificate of narrative faithfulness or fairness. Test labels must match intended semantics of edits.
relevance: Separates perturbations that should preserve labels from those that should change them.
baseline_use: Use framework to design targeted robustness/negative-control probes rather than claiming all perturbations should keep predictions unchanged.

title: FitCF: A Framework for Automatic Feature Importance-guided Counterfactual Example Generation
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025
status: Findings ACL2025 paper identified in official anthology metadata
access_depth: Official abstract and bibliographic metadata only; full text and code not retrieved
contribution: Introduces ZeroCF, attribution-important-word guidance for zero-shot counterfactual generation, and FitCF, which label-flip-verifies these candidates and inserts them as few-shot demonstrations; abstract discusses LIME/Integrated Gradients and ablations.
limitations: Only official abstract/metadata read; full protocol, target/generator identity, statistical results, prompt details and licensing not verified. Do not equate author use of faithful with established internal-faithfulness proof.
relevance: Very close prior art: attribution-guided generation plus label-flip verification is already expressly proposed.
baseline_use: Mandatory near-method comparison for any attribution-guided counterfactual proposal; inspect full text/code before finalizing protocol.

title: iFlip: Iterative Feedback-driven Counterfactual Example
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026
status: Official record labelled Findings EMNLP2026, October; publication timing/version not independently verified
access_depth: Official abstract and bibliographic metadata only; full text and code not retrieved
contribution: Iterative counterfactual refinement using model-confidence, attribution and natural-language feedback, with number-of-iterations, highly attributed words and early stopping identified as important in the abstract.
limitations: October2026 anthology record only; no DOI assigned in accessed metadata. Exact publication/version timing, full protocol, effect-size denominators, human study and code/licence have not been verified. No numeric performance result adopted from abstract.
relevance: Very close candidate prior art to attribution-guided iterative validation, feedback and bounded early stopping; novelty must be checked against it.
baseline_use: Inspect full text/code and establish release timing; include as nearest related method where reproducible rather than claim iterative feedback itself is new.
